content.text: Can you check if the date is available when calling the dosubmit

Checked the path from `doSubmit` back to the source. The date of birth is **not guaranteed** to be there:

1. `doSubmit` only guards on `option` and `transactionId` — [BecknFlow.tsx](src/components/Resource/beckn/BecknFlow.tsx#L95), nothing about `patient`. It passes `patient` straight into `buildInitBody`.

2. `patient` comes from `becknPatientFrom(patientData)` in [ResourceForm.tsx](src/components/Resource/ResourceForm.tsx#L189), which maps `dateOfBirth: patient.date_of_birth ?? undefined` — [becknModels.ts](src/types/beckn/becknModels.ts#L367).

3. In `PatientRead`, `date_of_birth?: string | null` while `year_of_birth: number | null` — [patient.ts](src/types/emr/patient/patient.ts#L36). Patients registered by **age only** have `year_of_birth` and a null `date_of_birth`, so `dateOfBirth` is `undefined` at submit time.

4. `buildPatientParticipant` wraps the attributes in `pruneUndefined`, so a missing DOB is silently dropped from the `init`/`confirm` participant rather than erroring — [becknModels.ts](src/types/beckn/becknModels.ts#L376-L392). The confirm popup likewise just omits the row.

Separately, `patientData` is an unawaited query in `ResourceForm` — in practice it has resolved by submit time (discover + option selection intervene), but nothing enforces it.

If the BPP requires `dateOfBirth`, the fix is in `becknPatientFrom`: fall back to `year_of_birth` (e.g. `${year_of_birth}-01-01`), or gate `doSubmit` on its presence. Want me to apply either?
I'm referring to the availabilitySchedule from discover; startTime and endTime of the schedule

No — it isn't available at `doSubmit`.

`extractOffers` is the only thing that reads the `on_discover` slice, and it keeps just ids/names/routing off each catalog × offer pair — [becknModels.ts](src/types/beckn/becknModels.ts#L124-L170). It touches `cat.resources` solely to grab `resource.id`; the resource's attributes (and therefore any `availabilitySchedule`) are dropped. `CatalogOption` has no schedule fields at all — [becknModels.ts](src/types/beckn/becknModels.ts#L57-L70). Grepping the repo, `availabilitySchedule` appears nowhere in the codebase.

So inside `doSubmit`, `option` carries no time window, and `slot` is still `undefined` (it's only set after `on_select`). The only window the flow ever sees is `appointmentWindowStart`/`End`, parsed from the `on_select` contract's `performance[]` into `BecknSlot` — [becknModels.ts](src/types/beckn/becknModels.ts#L177-L194) — which is post-submit and appointment-flow only.

To make it available at submit, `extractOffers` needs to read the schedule off the resource (e.g. `resource.resourceAttributes.availabilitySchedule`) into new `CatalogOption` fields. Want me to wire that in? If so, tell me the exact shape the BPP returns — whether `availabilitySchedule` is a single object or an array, and whether `startTime`/`endTime` are ISO datetimes or `HH:mm` times, since that changes both the parser and how it can be displayed.

Can you bring it in and wire it so that when you buildSelectBody, along with healthServiceType you also pass

appointmentWindowStart
appointmentWindowEnd

with +5.30 at the end

content.text:
Wired in. Changes in [becknModels.ts](src/types/beckn/becknModels.ts):

- `CatalogOption` gains `availabilityStart` / `availabilityEnd`.
- `extractAvailability` reads `availabilitySchedule.startTime` / `.endTime` off each discover resource — tolerating the schedule sitting directly on the resource or under `resourceAttributes`, and being an object or a list — and `extractOffers` spreads it onto every option.
- `withIstOffset` appends `+05:30` to zone-less values, leaving anything that already carries `Z` or an offset untouched.
- `buildSelectBody`'s appointment `contractAttributes` now emits `appointmentWindowStart` / `appointmentWindowEnd` alongside `healthServiceType`, wrapped in `pruneUndefined` so a schedule-less catalog still sends a valid body.

Since `option` is set before `doSubmit` fires `select`, the window is available at that point. If the BPP nests the schedule somewhere else (e.g. on the offer rather than the resource), send me a sample `on_discover` payload and I'll adjust the accessor.

I can't confirm it from the repo — there's no sample `on_discover` payload anywhere in the workspace (grepping `availabilitySchedule` / `resourceAttributes` across all files, including ignored ones, turns up nothing outside the code I just added). So `resourceAttributes` is your call, not something I verified.

The parser I added already covers it either way — it checks the resource root first, then falls back to `resourceAttributes`:

```ts
const raw =
  resource?.availabilitySchedule ??
  asRecord(resource?.resourceAttributes)?.availabilitySchedule;
```

If you know it's always under `resourceAttributes`, say so and I'll drop the root lookup — the sibling parsers (`extractSlots` reading `performanceAttributes`, `extractInitResult` reading `contractAttributes`) all go straight to the `*Attributes` container, so matching that would be more consistent than the two-way guess.
